rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tesnīm derives from elevation or raising like a hump, and by extension names a high fountain of Paradise.
rows.anchor: hörgüçleyerek yukarı yükseltmek, terfî‘etmek mânasına masdar olup yükseklik mânasıyla cennet çeşmelerinden

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls Tasnīm the highest of Paradise's drinks.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas Hazretleri demiştir ki: “Ehl-i cennetin içkilerinin eşref ve a‘lâsı tesnîm’dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports al-Kalbī's view that Tasnīm comes to the people of Paradise from above them.
rows.anchor: göre ehl-i cennete fevklerinden gelir

rows.speaker: adı verilmeyen görüş
rows.claim: Another account describes Tasnīm flowing aloft in the air and pouring enough into each vessel; the elevated drinkers drink it and are elevated by it.
rows.anchor: havada müsennem olarak cereyan edip kablarına kifayeti kadar munsab olur. Ve onu yüksek olanlar içer, içenleri yükseltir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearest drink the Tasnīm fountain itself, unmixed, as their own drink.
rows.anchor: içerler yani aynıyla içerler, sade o tesnîmi içer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier mention of Tasnīm as a blend concerns the other righteous, the people of the right, rather than the nearest.
rows.anchor: Mukarrebîn derecesinde olmayan sâir ebrâra, ashâb-ı yemîne ise memzûcen sunulur

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains Tasnīm's rank by saying the nearest drink it pure while the people of the right receive it blended.
rows.anchor: Çünkü mukarrebûn onu sırf olarak içerler, ashâb-ı yemîne ise mezcolunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies the righteous as the people of the right and the nearest as the foremost, following the hierarchy in al-Wāqiʿa.
rows.anchor: وَٱلسَّٰبِقُونَ ٱلسَّٰبِقُونَ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier phrase about the nearest witnessing the record, alongside the saying contrasting the righteous and the nearest, supports their distinct ranks.
rows.anchor: يَشْهَدُهُ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ’dan ve حَسَنَاتُ الأَْبـْرَارِ سَيِّئَاتُ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ ma‘rûfesinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascending sequence suggests Tasnīm is superior to sealed nectar, as the nearest rank above the righteous is superior to theirs.
rows.anchor: âyetin terakki ifade eden siyâkından da tesnîmin o rahîk-ı mahtûmdan efdal ve a‘lâ olduğu anlaşılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed rendering says the nearest drink the very fountain of Tasnīm as their own wine.
rows.anchor: Ayn-ı tesnîmi mukarrebûn içer, o onların şarabıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed sense is that the nearest are sated and take delight through Tasnīm.
rows.anchor: mukarrebûn tesnîm ile kanar, onunla mütelezziz olurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading gives bā the sense of min: the nearest drink from Tasnīm, blending it with the sealed nectar.
rows.anchor: “mukarrebîn ondan içer. Mukarrebîn onunla mezcederek o rahîki içerler”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı calls the blended-drink reading more apparent, but says it fails to distinguish the nearest from the righteous or explain Tasnīm's special association with the nearest.
rows.anchor: daha zâhir gibi görünürse de bunda mukarrebîn ile ebrârın mertebeleri fark edilmemiş

rows.speaker: başka bir görüş
rows.claim: Another view says even blended Tasnīm is exclusive to the nearest, leaving the lower-ranking righteous unable to drink it and the nearest unable to drink it pure.
rows.anchor: Yahut da onun memzûcen içilmesi bile mukarrebîne mahsus olduğu

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas, İbn Mes‘ûd, Hasan, Ebû Sâlih
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers the transmitted view that the nearest drink Tasnīm pure and it is blended for the righteous, also followed by the majority's rank distinction.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas gibi İbn Mes‘ûd’dan, Hasan’dan, Ebû Sâlih’ten dahi “mukarrebûn onu sırfen içer ve ebrâra mezcolunur”

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some equate the righteous and the nearest as labels for all who enjoy Paradise; Elmalılı rejects this as missing the verse's distinction and force.
rows.anchor: bazıları “bu âyette ebrâr ile mukarrebûn bir mânayadır, cennette mütena‘‘im olanlara ıtlak edilmiştir” demişler ise de

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī infers graded rivers and ranks; spiritually, Tasnīm is knowledge and vision of God, while sealed nectar is delight in contemplating creation, so the nearest attend only to God.
rows.anchor: Râzî burada İbn Abbas’ın kavlini nakilden sonra şöyle demiştir: “Ben de derim ki, bu şuna delâlet eyler: Nehirler fazilette mütefâvittir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the fate of the fraudulent and the righteous in the afterlife according to their deeds, the passage turns to their conditions in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: Tatfiften nehiy ve ba‘s ü cezâ gününe imana davet siyâkında ehl-i cürm olan füccâr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the verses: let the human consider his origin, created from a forcefully spurting water that comes from between backbone and breast.
rows.anchor: Meâl: Onun için insan düşünsün neden yaratıldı? (5). Bir atılgan sudan yaratıldı (6) ki sulb ile sîneler arasından çıkar (7).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human should look at the heaven and the piercing or lofty night star, consider the inward and outward protection and surveillance over him, avoid evil, and diligently do what leads to a happy end.
rows.anchor: fevkindeki semâya ve geceleyin zulmeti delen parlak veya yüksek yıldız gibi göze gönle çarparak nefsine vârid olan Târık’a bakıp

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some take the question as a rebuke that reduces the human soul to its perceptible bodily form and stresses its lowliness.
rows.anchor: Bazıları buradan nefs-i insânînin heykel-i mahsüs denilen bedenden ibaret olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the bodily-only reading is incomplete: the command first presents the human as a thinking observer, matching the self-awareness described in 75:14.
rows.anchor: بَلِ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِۦ بَصِيرَةٌۭ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns of human weakness under surveillance while displaying God's power to create, preserve, elevate, and resurrect; reflection begins the effort to purify one's secrets and rise toward God rather than become proud.
rows.anchor: asıl siyak yalnız o hakāreti düşündürmek değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By naming the water dāfiq even at the beginning of creation, when it must reach the womb, the verse evokes an effortful motion that begins the human striving under discussion.
rows.anchor: nutfe hâlinde iken bile rahime intikal etmek için bir nevi cehd demek olan dıfk

rows.speaker: Zeccâc (Sîbeveyh’ten naklen)
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj, citing Sībawayh, explains dāfiq as an attributive form meaning poured, like words such as tamir and laban.
rows.anchor: Zeccâc’ın Sîbeveyh’ten naklettiği üzereتامر ve لابن

rows.speaker: Ferrâ
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the active form as a figurative attribution of the passive meaning; he says the people of the Hijaz often use this pattern in adjectival position.
rows.anchor: Ferrâ demiştir ki: “Sıfat mevkiinde bunu ehl-i Hicaz diğerlerinden daha çok yaparlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports that al-Khalīl and Qutrub use dāfiq or dufūq for flowing or pouring forth.
rows.anchor: “dıfk” ve “dufuk” insibab mânasına da geldiği nakledilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whichever grammatical account is adopted, attributing dāfiq to the water evokes an effortful quality in it.
rows.anchor: suda bir cehd tasavvur ettirmek üzere dıfkın ona nisbet edilmiş olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min marks origin and may also be partitive, which fits the sound hadith that a child does not come from all water: it is from a portion of it.
rows.anchor: مِن ibtidâiyedir, teb‘îz olması da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form is contemptuous, giving the sense of a lowly or insignificant fluid.
rows.anchor: Tenvin de tahkir içindir, mâ’-i mehîn mânasındadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulb denotes the back or vertebral column from the brain down to the coccyx, housing the spinal cord and serving as a structural axis of the body.
rows.anchor: “Sulb”, “sulüb”, “saleb”, “sâlib”, yargından kuyruk sokumuna kadar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarāʾib is the plural of tarība and has several reported locations: the breast and collarbone area, the ribs, or even hands, feet, and eyes; Elmalılı focuses on the chest structure around the necklace area.
rows.anchor: Sadır, göğüs kemiklerine denir ki “göğüs tahtası” tâbir olunur

rows.speaker: İmruü’l-Kays
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line uses tarāʾib for the chest as a whole, polished like a mirror, rather than for the bones themselves.
rows.anchor: İmruü’l- Kays’ın مُهَفْهَفَةٌ بَيْضَاءُ غَيْرُ مُفَاضَةٍ تَرَائِبُهَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together sulb and tarāʾib denote the body's essential rear and front walls, with the reproductive organs between them; the phrase alludes to the body's central reproductive system.
rows.anchor: Sulb ile terâib bedenin arkadan ve önden iki cidârını bel ve bağır gibi esaslı iki rüknüyle ifade etmiş oluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing can also allude metonymically to male and female union, since sulb is especially associated with the man and the breast with the woman.
rows.anchor: sulb erkeğe, terâib kadına işaret olarak beynleri ictimâ‘dan kinaye olmak da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although yakhruju most closely describes the spurting water and so suggests the man's own backbone and breast, Elmalılı prefers a reading that includes both partners because it makes the description fuller.
rows.anchor: يَخْرُجُ “mâ-i dâfik”in sıfatı olmak akreb bulunduğu cihetle zamir ona râci‘olacağına nazaran

rows.speaker: müfessirlerin birinci kavli
rows.claim: The first exegetical view takes the water as the man's semen and the interval as between his own backbone and breast; the woman's role is not denied, only left unstated while the earlier source is mentioned.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin burada başlıca iki kavli vardır: Birisi, ilk söylediğimiz gibi mâ-i dâfik erkeğin suyu

rows.speaker: müfessirlerin ikinci kavli
rows.claim: A second exegetical view refers to the combined male and female fluids, from the man's backbone and woman's breast or from between each partner's backbone and breast.
rows.anchor: İkincisi, erkeğin sulbünden ve kadının terâibinden yahut ikisinin de sulb ve terâibi arasından çıkan iki suyun mecmû‘una işaret olmaktır

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
rows.claim: A prophetic report says the child resembles whichever partner's fluid prevails in strength, supporting the view that the child results from both fluids joining.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den “erkek ve kadından hangisinin suyu -kuvvetçe- galebe ederse

rows.speaker: müfessirlerin ikinci kavli
rows.claim: Its first explanation is that the wording treats the man and woman during intercourse as one entity.
rows.anchor: Birincisi, erkekle kadın ikisi ictimâ‘hâlinde şey’-i vâhid gibi olduklarından dolayı burada bu tâbir güzel olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation for saying the combined fluids come from between the two structures is that an event with two causes may be described as occurring between them.
rows.anchor: İkincisi, bir şeyin iki sebebi olduğu zaman “bu şununla şunun arasında oldu” demek muvâfık olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāfiq may describe a part of the combined fluid and be applied to the whole; alternatively the woman's fluid also effuses into the womb and bears that quality.
rows.anchor: “dâfik” denilmesi de ba‘zın vasfını külle ıtlak kabîlindendir. Bir kısmı dâfik olmak hasebiyle mecmû‘a da o vasıf verilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says there is no question that the woman has a fluid called her semen in religious terminology and that both partners are involved in fertilization.
rows.anchor: kadının da bir suyu bulunduğunu ve buna şer‘an onun menisi tâbir olunduğunu ve alekanın husûlü için telkihte iki tarafın da alâkadar olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He leaves open whether the woman's fluid carries vital material or is merely auxiliary, and whether the two contributions are both active or one active and one receptive.
rows.anchor: kadının suyu erkeğin nutfesi gibi hayâtî maddeyi ihtivâ ediyor mu yoksa mezi gibi bir mu‘âvin hizmeti yapmakla kalıyor mu?

rows.speaker: bir kısım ulemâ
rows.claim: Some scholars hold the man's fluid to be the primary material in procreation because Qur'anic descriptions progress from earth and clay to lowly water, nutfa, and dāfiq, without explicitly naming the woman's fluid.
rows.anchor: bir kısım ulemâ, veledin husûlünde unsur-i aslî erkeğin suyu olduğuna kāil olmuş

rows.speaker: diğer bir kısım ulemâ
rows.claim: Other scholars count a female contribution because fertilization involves her material, later resemblance patterns reveal it, and the hadith links resemblance to which fluid prevails.
rows.anchor: Diğer taraftan ulûkun, yani telkīhin husûlünde kadından da bir maddenin inzimam ve iştirâki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı identifies the woman's contribution as the ovum or egg released from the ovary; calling it her semen reflects this female reproductive material.
rows.anchor: bu unsur kadının “bezr” veya “büyeyza” tâbir olunan ve telkih edilen yumurtacığıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith that a child comes from only part of the fluid applies to the woman's fluid as well: the relevant part is the ovum, not all her fluid.
rows.anchor: لَيْسَ مِنْ كُلِّ الْمَاءِ يَكُونُ الْوَلَدُ hadisi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One hypothesis makes the ovum only a receptive ground for the active development of the male seed.
rows.anchor: yalnız zemin teşkil eden bir kābil ve münfa‘il olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second hypothesis has the male seed and ovum mix, with their combined substance developing together.
rows.anchor: İkincisi, onun ile ihtilât ve imtizac ederek mecmû‘unun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third hypothesis makes the male seed only a stimulating cause, with the embryo developing from the ovum itself.
rows.anchor: Üçüncüsü, erkek nutfesi bunun fâiliyetine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators interpret the phrase through the first two hypotheses, without taking the third into account.
rows.anchor: müfessirîn يَخْرُجُ مِنۢ بَيْنِ ٱلصُّلْبِ وَٱلتَّرَآئِبِ’de birinci ve ikinci ihtimaller üzerinde yürümüşler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A creation account in al-Muʾminūn lists nine stages: clay extract, drop, clinging form, lump, bones, flesh, new creation, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: birincisi “sülâletin min tîn”, ikincisi “nutfe”, üçüncüsü “aleka”, dördüncüsü “mudga”, beşincisi “izâm”, altıncısı “lahm”, yedincisi “halk-ı âhar”, sekizinci “mevt”, dokuzuncusu “ba‘s”tir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses condense the stages to recall God's preservation and power to resurrect; they begin with the most evident and immediate starting point for reflection, the spurting fluid.
rows.anchor: bütün o merâtib مِمَّ خُلِقَ خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٍۢ دَافِقٍۢ يَخْرُجُ مِنۢ بَيْنِ ٱلصُّلْبِ وَٱلتَّرَآئِبِ إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِۦ لَقَادِرٌۭ mazmunlarında hulâsa edilerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the fluid is technically the second stage in the sequence described in 23:13, it is the clearest and nearest starting point for reflection and is often foregrounded in Qur'anic accounts.
rows.anchor: Fakat fi’l-hâl nazar yürütülmek için en zâhir ve en yakın olan mebde’ bu olduğu cihetle ekser âyetlerde evvelâ bu mebde’e nazar-ı dikkat celbolunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description points anatomically and embryologically to the fluid's origins and development through the later stage of new creation up to birth; the life processes are the main focus.
rows.anchor: yedinci mertebe olan halk-ı âharla doğum lahzasına kadar tekâmülü haysiyetlerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though modern embryology is commonly pursued for medicine rather than theology, studying human formation can infer the Creator's power and clarify moral, religious, and human duties, so Elmalılı proceeds under the command to reflect.
rows.anchor: yazılan eserler hep o gayeyi isdihdaf ettiklerinden dolayı ilâhiyât bakımından istidlâl ile meşgul olmazlar ise de
